a point mutation at the endmost C terminal position of the BHA cytoplasmic region, which is hydrophobic in the wild-type protein, inhibits syncytial formation.
the endmost Leu of the C termini of BHA does not contribute directly to the fusion activity of this protein, but that its hydrophobicity is crucial to syncytium formation.
the endmost Leu residue of BHA is not essential for fusion, but that hydrophobicity at this position is crucial.

the role of the C termini of influenza B virus hemagglutinins in membrane fusion.
the molecular mechanisms of membrane fusion and the development of a new antiviral strategy against influenza B virus.
the molecular basis of the syncytium formation by influenza virus.

a single hydrophobic amino residue at the C termini of the HA2 subunit of influenza B and A virus is not essential for membrane-fusion activity, but that it plays a crucial role for syncytium formation.

the endmost Leu of the C-terminal sequence of BHA-CT does not contribute to the membrane-fusion ability but that its hydrophobicity does.

the C-terminal hydrophobic amino-acid sequence is not required for BHA-mediated membrane fusion, but the endmost hydrophobic amino residue plays an important role for the fusion process, and the C-terminal amino-acid sequence of BHA-CT may be involved in the fusion process in a different way from that of HA-CT.
